about: The starter rulebook: universal coding-agent rules whose repo-specific parts are {{slots}} filled by starter_rulebook.py from a scan of the checkout. `requires` names the slots a rule cannot exist without; a rule whose slot is missing is dropped, never filed with a guess. `cases` are run through the live hook's engine after seeding. Patterns match at command position ({{CMD}} / {{GIT}}), never `^`; paths match `(?:^|/)dir/` because the hook sees absolute paths; no quantified group contains + * or | because the hook's load lint drops those. `same_as` names the session miner's built-in hypothesis (mine_sessions.py) that covers the same ground under a different title and pattern: the deterministic conflict check cannot see those, so both skills read this list. Rules with `given.user` share one limit: `said_rx` / `not_said_rx` see every user turn of the session, unordered, so they cannot tell an approval that came before a request from one that came after. Every such rule is written to fail OPEN on that ambiguity (stay silent), never to block. An ordering rule's `scope_paths` / `scope_exclude_paths` say which edits arm it; the hook honours them from 0.74.0, so every path-scoped gate carries that floor and an older hook advises instead of blocking on an edit the rule was never about.

categories.name: Context budget
categories.ask: Keep big files, diffs and listings out of the main agent's context
categories.blurb: Input far larger than the answer is read as a slice or handed to a delegate. Reads are 46-76% of agent tokens; Spotify measured 82-94% savings from the same 350-line gate.

categories.name: Cheap verification
categories.ask: Stop the agent burning minutes on full test suites, installs and dev servers
categories.blurb: The touched test while editing, the suite once before push. Agents run tests ~8.8 times per task for ~1 point of benefit.

categories.name: Test hygiene
categories.ask: Stop tests being skipped, slowed or snapshot-updated to get green
categories.blurb: Matched against the content about to be written, so a slow or skipped test is caught while it is authored.

categories.name: Safety
categories.ask: Block irreversible git, deletes, secrets, production and hook tampering
categories.blurb: Irreversible operations, secrets and production. Designed as gates: the override records the reason, which is the audit trail.

categories.name: Infrastructure pack
categories.ask: Block destructive Docker / Terraform / Kubernetes / AWS commands
categories.blurb: Enabled only where the scan finds the tool in the repo.

categories.name: Runtime traps
categories.ask: Stop calls that hang, never return, or poll with sleep
categories.blurb: A hung call wastes a turn; an unbounded one wastes context.

categories.name: Repo hygiene
categories.ask: Commit discipline, dependencies, lockfiles, migrations, PR size

categories.name: Intent alignment
categories.ask: Make the agent do what was asked: answer questions, plan when told to plan, reproduce before fixing
categories.blurb: Fires on the gap between what the person typed and what the agent is about to do.

categories.name: Subagent guardrails
categories.ask: Keep subagents from pushing, installing, or touching CI, infra and databases
categories.blurb: What makes delegation safe enough to push work toward it.

categories.name: Posture and anchors
categories.ask: Four session-start lines plus reminders on this repo's heaviest files
categories.blurb: Session-start statements shape the plan before any rule fires. Expect partial compliance; they explain the gates rather than replace them.

rules.title: Read large files as a slice
rules.statement: This file is over {{read_threshold}} lines. Read the section you need with offset and limit. Delegate only a multi-file question, and to a cheaper model.
rules.why: a whole-file read is re-sent on every later turn; a same-model subagent costs ~54K tokens to start, so slicing beats delegating for one file.
rules.seeded_from: largest files: threshold is the repo's p95 file length, clamped to 350-500
rules.evidence: Spotify shunt ships this exact gate at 350 lines

rules.title: Never read lockfiles or build output
rules.statement: Lockfiles, build output, vendored and minified code are not read whole. Grep for the one line you need.
rules.why: these files carry no reasoning value per token.
rules.seeded_from: .gitignore build and cache entries, plus every lockfile shape

rules.title: Query large data files
rules.statement: Large data file. Use jq, head, or a short script for the shape or the count you need.
rules.why: data files are read for a shape or a count, not for their content.

rules.title: Do not read binary files
rules.statement: Binary archive or database. There is nothing to read as text. Use the tool for the type, or skip it.
rules.why: a binary read is pure noise for every agent.

rules.title: Stat a large diff first
rules.statement: The branch diff is over 400 lines. Run git diff --stat here and read it by file, or delegate the review one subagent per dimension.
rules.why: fires exactly when reading the diff costs the most. Only the whole-branch form: a diff narrowed to a path (`-- file`) or sent to a file is the advice already taken, and `git show <commit>` is that commit's size, not the branch's.

rules.title: Bound git history reads
rules.statement: Bound it: git log -n 20 --oneline, git blame -L start,end.
rules.why: history is the one input with no natural end.

rules.title: Bound listings and logs
rules.statement: Add a bound: tree -L 2, docker logs --tail 100, journalctl -n 100, or pipe through head.
rules.why: recursive listings, dependency trees and container logs print until the buffer ends.

rules.title: Subagents slice huge files too
rules.statement: Even in a delegate, a file this long makes a worse answer. Slice it.
rules.why: a subagent context is disposable, not free.

rules.title: Run targeted tests while editing
rules.statement: Edits are uncommitted. Run the test file for what you changed; leave the whole suite for CI or one run before push.
rules.why: a bare suite run in the inner loop is the most common verification waste.
rules.seeded_from: toolchain: the repo's test command family
rules.evidence: agents run tests 8.8x per task; prohibiting execution cost 1.25 points

rules.title: Lint before the test run
rules.statement: Run the linter before the suite. Syntax and type errors surface in a second, not after collection.
rules.why: cheap check before expensive check. No study shows an ordering benefit, so this advises and never blocks.
rules.seeded_from: lint tooling: the repo entrypoint (make lint) when one exists, else raw tool names

rules.title: Lint before push
rules.statement: Edits are in flight and the linter has not run green. Run it before anything leaves the machine, because CI will.
rules.why: CI parity: a lint failure found in CI costs a round trip.
rules.seeded_from: lint tooling

rules.title: Run tests green before push
rules.statement: Edits are in flight and no test run has come back green since. Run the tests for what you changed (the whole suite if it is quick) before anything leaves the machine.
rules.why: a push with no green run since the last edit is the cheapest failure to prevent. Any green test run clears it, targeted included: forcing a full local suite duplicates CI, and on a slow suite is how a rule gets switched off. A docs-only edit never arms it: the suite cannot fail because of prose, and the non-code rule says to skip it.
rules.seeded_from: toolchain / CI: the repo's test command
rules.evidence: Spotify Honk runs the same verifier loop before a PR opens

rules.title: Skip the suite for non-code diffs
rules.statement: Nothing changed on this branch is source code. The suite cannot fail because of it; skip it and say so.
rules.why: docs-only and config-only branches do not need the test run they usually get.
rules.seeded_from: toolchain: the repo's source extensions

rules.title: Skip installs when manifests are unchanged
rules.statement: No manifest changed on this branch. Unless this is a fresh checkout or worktree, the environment is already current: install only if an import fails.
rules.why: installs are slow and print a lot.
rules.seeded_from: manifests: the manifest and lockfile names present

rules.title: Do not boot the app to verify
rules.statement: Verify with a unit test or a one-shot script. If you must run the app, background it and bring back the response, not the log.
rules.why: booting the app and tailing logs is the most expensive way to check a change.
rules.seeded_from: dev server config: Dockerfile CMD, compose services, dev scripts

rules.title: Run slow tiers only when asked
rules.statement: Nobody asked for the slow tier or coverage. Run the unit tier and say what you skipped.
rules.why: the expensive markers exist so they can be skipped.
rules.seeded_from: test markers: the repo's own marker names, and the same words for what the person must have said

rules.title: Notice a slow test run
rules.statement: That run took over 100 seconds. Next time narrow to the changed test file, or background the full run.
rules.why: the hook cannot time a command, but the runner prints its duration. 100s is a placeholder: recalibrate from fire history.

rules.title: No sleep or network in unit tests
rules.statement: Unit tests mock the boundary: no real sleeps or HTTP calls. Put a test that needs them under the integration directory.
rules.why: caught while the test is written, which is the only cheap moment to fix it. Subprocess calls are deliberately not matched: replayed on a CLI codebase, every fire was a legitimate test of the CLI itself.
rules.seeded_from: test layout: the test root, with integration directories excluded by path

rules.title: Real databases belong in integration tests
rules.statement: A live database connection in the unit tier. Use the fixture here, and cover the real database in an integration test, which must exist.
rules.why: a real connection is the difference between a two-second suite and a two-minute one; agents already over-mock, so the integration test matters.
rules.seeded_from: migrations dir: present only when the repo has a database layer

rules.title: A source change needs a test
rules.statement: Source changed on this branch and no test did. Add one, or say in the PR why none is needed.
rules.why: fires at the exit, where the omission is cheapest to notice.
rules.seeded_from: test layout: the source roots and the test root

rules.title: Never skip a test to get green
rules.statement: A failing test is not fixed by skipping it. Fix the code, or ask.
rules.why: the most tempting shortcut under pressure; allowed only when the person asked for it.
rules.evidence: reward hacking runs 12-18% on prone tasks

user_said: skip that flaky test for now

rules.title: Never regenerate snapshots unasked
rules.statement: Updating snapshots accepts whatever the code does now. Read the snapshot diff first, and update only when asked.
rules.why: a snapshot update is a test deletion that looks like a fix.

rules.title: Stop irreversible git operations
rules.statement: This rewrites or discards history or stashed work. Use the reversible form (--force-with-lease on your own branch, a commit on a scratch branch) or say why through the override.
rules.why: an undone action is the most expensive turn there is; filter-repo plus a force push caused a documented production outage. `branch -D` is left out: the reflog recovers it, and agents delete their own scratch branches constantly.
rules.evidence: matches every hook collection surveyed and Anthropic's own hook examples

rules.title: Stop git commands that discard uncommitted work
rules.statement: This throws away uncommitted work across the tree, and nothing records it. Commit or stash first, name the one file, or say why through the override.
rules.why: the reflog keeps commits, not edits: a tree-wide checkout, restore, clean or a forced worktree removal is the one git loss with no undo. A dry run (`git clean -n`) and a single named file are left alone.

rules.title: Never bypass commit hooks
rules.statement: --no-verify, HUSKY=0 and core.hooksPath switch off the repo's own checks. Fix what the hook found, or ask.
rules.why: one documented session landed six commits with 63 failing tests this way, despite a written rule against it.

user_said: commit with --no-verify, the hook is broken

silent.case: git commit -m 'cli: add -n flag for dry run'

rules.title: Look before a recursive delete
rules.statement: Recursive delete. Check what the target expands to first (an empty variable deletes its parent); for repo files prefer git clean -n, then delete.
rules.why: advises rather than blocks: replayed over real sessions, recursive deletes are overwhelmingly scratch cleanup, and a gate that fires that often gets overridden by habit.

rules.title: Never recursively delete home or root
rules.statement: This recursive delete targets a home directory, the filesystem root, a system directory, a parent directory or a bare glob. Stop: name the exact directory instead.
rules.why: the three documented home-directory wipes all had this shape; there is no legitimate agent task that needs it.

rules.title: Look before a bulk delete by another tool
rules.statement: This deletes in bulk without rm. Check what it matches first (run the find without -delete), then delete.
rules.why: find -delete, find -exec rm, xargs rm and rmtree are how a delete gets past an rm rule. Advises for the same reason the rm rule does: replayed, these are overwhelmingly cache and scratch cleanup, and a gate that fires that often gets overridden by habit.

rules.title: Never write to a raw device
rules.statement: This writes to a raw device or makes a filesystem on one. Stop and confirm with the person.
rules.why: dd to /dev and mkfs erase a disk, not a directory; no agent task needs either unasked.

rules.title: No direct push to the default branch
rules.statement: You are on the default branch. Work on a branch and open a PR.
rules.why: the most common written team rule, and one of the few that is fully deterministic. Only a push of the CURRENT branch: an explicitly named other ref (`git push origin feat/x`) does not touch the default branch, and one that names it is the companion rule's. A token that starts a redirect (`2>&1`) or another command (`&& gh pr create`) is not a ref: the first version read them as one and went silent on the commonest push there is.
rules.seeded_from: default branch, from origin/HEAD, anchored exactly. No origin/HEAD, no rule: a guessed `main` would leave a `trunk` repo unguarded while looking guarded

fires.case: cd api && git push origin HEAD
git push origin HEAD && echo done
git push -u origin HEAD; git status

rules.title: No pushing to the default branch by name
rules.statement: This push names the default branch as its destination (or deletes it). Push your own branch and open a PR.
rules.why: `git push origin HEAD:{{default_branch}}` lands on the default branch from any checkout, and `--delete {{default_branch}}` removes it; a rule that only looks at the current branch sees neither.
rules.seeded_from: default branch, from origin/HEAD

fires.case: cd api && git push origin feat/x:refs/heads/{{default_branch}}

rules.title: Stop destructive database operations
rules.statement: Drops, truncates, unscoped deletes and downgrades stop here. Say which database and why through the override.
rules.why: cheap to type, impossible to undo without a backup. A commit message or a PR body that mentions the words is not a database call; lower-case `truncate` alone is English.
rules.seeded_from: migrations dir: the repo's migration tool and its destructive verbs

fires: git commit -m 'wip: x' && psql -c 'DROP TABLE users'
silent: gh pr create --title 'x' --body 'We truncate long tool outputs'
gh issue comment 5 --body 'do not drop table users'
git commit -m 'drop table cleanup' && git push

rules.title: Never read secrets
rules.statement: Secrets never enter the context. Read the example file, or ask for the variable name.
rules.why: a secret in a transcript is a rotation. Also add these paths to permissions.deny, which holds in every permission mode.
rules.seeded_from: .gitignore secret patterns and .env templates

rules.title: Never dump the environment
rules.statement: Print the one variable you need, never the whole environment or an env file.
rules.why: a secret leak and a noise dump in one command.

rules.title: Never stage secrets or build output
rules.statement: That path does not belong in the repo. Check the ignore file and stage by name.
rules.why: a committed secret costs a rotation; a committed build directory costs every clone. Bulk forms (`git add -A`) never name the file, so they are a separate rule that reads the branch's changed paths.
rules.seeded_from: the same secret set the read gate uses (.gitignore patterns and .env templates), shaped for a command line

rules.title: No stage-everything over an unignored secret
rules.statement: A secret or key file on this branch is not ignored, and `git add -A` stages the whole tree from any directory. Add it to .gitignore, or stage by name.
rules.why: `git add -A` never names the file it sweeps in, so a rule that looks for `.env` in the command cannot see it; the branch's changed paths can. `git add -u` and `git commit -a` are left out on purpose: they touch tracked files only, so they cannot stage the untracked secret this rule is about.
rules.seeded_from: .gitignore secret patterns and .env templates, matched against the branch's changed and untracked paths

rules.title: No `git add .` over an unignored secret
rules.statement: A secret or key file on this branch is not ignored, and `git add .` stages everything under this directory. Add it to .gitignore, or stage by name.
rules.why: `.` is a pathspec, not the whole tree: it reaches only what is under the directory the command runs in. So this fires only when the command changes directory nowhere (`cd`, `pushd`, `git -C`) — then `.` is as wide as the repo is from here. If the shell was already left in a subdirectory by an earlier call it can still over-fire; the override records why.
rules.seeded_from: .gitignore secret patterns and .env templates, matched against the branch's changed and untracked paths

fires.case: git status && git add . && git commit -m 'x: y'

rules.title: Production is not a place to verify
rules.statement: Production context. Stop and confirm with the person before anything runs against it.
rules.why: the structural fix is dev/prod separation; this is the tripwire until then.
rules.seeded_from: CI workflows: the deploy and release workflow names

rules.title: Never pipe a download into a shell
rules.statement: Download it, read it, then run it.
rules.why: the one supply-chain rule that costs nothing to enforce. The installer forms count too: `bash -c "$(curl …)"`, `bash <(curl …)`, a `tee` in the middle, and an interpreter reading the download from stdin.

rules.title: Do not edit your own guardrails
rules.statement: This file configures the agent's own hooks, permissions or CI. Propose the change and let the person make it, unless they asked for it.
rules.why: an agent that can rewrite its hooks and workflows can switch off every other rule in this book. `hooks` and `settings` on their own do not count as asking: a session about React hooks or a settings page says both.

user_said: fix the useAuth hooks in the settings page
add a CI workflow that runs the tests
add a claude hook that runs the linter

rules.title: No world-writable or recursive ownership changes
rules.statement: 777, setuid and recursive chown fix a permission error by removing the permission model. Grant the one bit the one file needs.
rules.why: the usual 'make the error go away' move, and it outlives the session.

rules.title: Stop destructive Docker cleanup
rules.statement: This deletes Docker volumes, which takes local databases with it. Name what and why through the override.
rules.why: a named volume is somebody's development database. Image and build-cache prunes are left alone: they cost a rebuild, not data.
rules.seeded_from: Dockerfile or compose file present

rules.title: Stop infrastructure teardown
rules.statement: This destroys cloud resources or skips the approval that would have caught it. Stop and confirm with the person.
rules.why: documented agent incidents include terminated instances and deleted databases; no local undo exists.
rules.seeded_from: Terraform files, Kubernetes manifests, or AWS CLI usage in CI

rules.title: No commands that wait for a keyboard
rules.statement: This waits for a keyboard that is not there. Use the non-interactive form: python -c, psql -c, git rebase without -i, git add by name.
rules.why: a hung call wastes the whole turn and often the session. A REPL at the end of a pipe (`echo … | python3`) reads stdin and returns, so only a bare one at command position counts.

rules.title: No git commands that open an editor
rules.statement: This opens an editor for the message and hangs. Pass it: git commit -m, git commit --amend --no-edit, git revert --no-edit.
rules.why: a hung call wastes the whole turn and often the session. `--fixup` writes its own message and is left alone.

rules.title: No watch modes in the foreground
rules.statement: This never returns. Run it once, or background it and let the harness wake you.
rules.why: same failure as a blocked terminal, with output attached. Advises rather than blocks because a backgrounded follower is legitimate and the hook cannot see the difference.

rules.title: Do not poll with sleep
rules.statement: Sleeping in the foreground spends a turn waiting. Background the job and let the harness wake you.
rules.why: polling loops are the quiet turn-eater.

fires: gh run watch; sleep 120 && gh run view
until curl -s localhost:8000; do sleep 5; done

rules.title: Narrow scope after a resource wall
rules.statement: The last call hit a resource or rate limit. Narrow the scope or background it; do not re-run it unchanged.
rules.why: output rules cannot prevent, but they teach the next call. Failed runs are 13-83% longer, mostly from retries.

matcher.content_rx: ^(?:Killed|MemoryError|OOMKilled)\b|^(?:npm ERR!|error:|Error:|fatal:|ERROR:?)[^\n]*(?:429 Too Many Requests|ETIMEDOUT|ENOSPC|No space left on device)

silent: cat notes.md::we saw the process get killed yesterday
cat report.md::| `429 Too Many Requests` | retried |

rules.title: Clean the tree before branch operations
rules.statement: Uncommitted changes. Stash them (or commit them, if the person asked for commits) before you pull, rebase, or switch.
rules.why: the cheapest merge conflict is the one that never starts; a documented postmortem lost work exactly here.

rules.title: Keep scratch files out of the repo
rules.statement: Scratch goes to the scratchpad or temp directory, not the repo.
rules.why: debug scripts and notes at the root end up in the commit.

rules.title: Stage by name on a wide branch
rules.statement: Many files changed on this branch. Stage by name so the commit is what you meant.
rules.why: git add -A on a wide branch is how scratch files and secrets get in. `git commit -a` is left out: it takes tracked files only, so it cannot sweep in either.

rules.title: Justify a new dependency
rules.statement: Editing a dependency manifest. If this adds a dependency, check the standard library and what is already installed first, and say why in the PR.
rules.why: every dependency is a supply-chain and install-time cost forever.

rules.title: Regenerate {{lock_name}} after its manifest changes
rules.statement: `{{lock_manifest}}` changed. Regenerate `{{lock_name}}` with `{{lock_cmd_example}}` before push; never edit it by hand.
rules.why: CI will reject a stale lock. One rule per lockfile, paired with the manifest in its own directory and its own tool, so neither another ecosystem's install nor another package's edit touches this one. Known limit: the receipt is the tool's command, not where it ran — two packages on the same tool clear each other.
rules.seeded_from: manifests: each lockfile found beside its manifest, paired with its own tool

rules.title: Generate migrations, do not hand-write them
rules.statement: Migration file. A new revision is generated with `{{mig_generate_hint}}` and then edited; never hand-number one.
rules.why: hand-numbered revisions are how two heads happen.
rules.seeded_from: migrations dir: the versions directory, not the tool directory, so an env.py edit stays quiet

rules.title: One migration head before push
rules.statement: A migration changed. Run `alembic heads` and confirm a single head before push.
rules.why: two heads block every deploy after the merge. The gate can see that the command ran, not what it printed: `alembic heads` exits 0 with two heads, so reading the output is on you.
rules.seeded_from: migrations dir: alembic

rules.title: Keep PRs reviewable
rules.statement: This branch is over 400 changed lines. Split it, or say in the description why it cannot be split.
rules.why: review defect detection falls above 200-400 lines; AI-written PRs over that size merge less than half as often.
rules.evidence: SmartBear 200-400 LOC; AI PRs average 408 LOC and merge within 30 days 33% vs 84%

fires.case: cd api && gh pr create --base main

rules.title: Do not commit unless asked
rules.statement: Nobody asked for a commit. Leave the changes in the tree and say they are ready.
rules.why: an unrequested commit is the most common autonomy overreach, and it is deterministic from what the person typed.

user_said: fix the parser bug and commit it

rules.title: Write commit messages that say something
rules.statement: One line on what changed and why. "fix" is not a message.
rules.why: cheap now, expensive at bisect time.

silent: git commit -m 'fix: parser drops the last token at eof'

rules.title: Regenerate generated files
rules.statement: This file is generated. Change the source and rerun the generator.
rules.why: a hand edit to a generated file is lost on the next regeneration.
rules.seeded_from: generated files: generated-by headers, plus known suffixes

rules.title: Answer a question before editing
rules.statement: They asked a question. Answer it first, and edit when asked.
rules.why: the most common scope creep: a how or a why turns into a patch. Scope creep shows up in ~10% of real sessions. `Can you…`, `could you…` and `should…` are left out: they are how people phrase a task.

rules.title: Plan only means no edits
rules.statement: The person asked for a plan. No edits until they say go.
rules.why: deterministic from the prompt; a written 'wait for approval' instruction was ignored in a documented incident. Known gap: the hook reads everything typed this session with no order, so an approval given EARLIER ('go ahead' on a previous task) also silences a later plan-only request. It fails open — it can miss, it cannot block work that was approved. A scoped prohibition (`don't touch the public API`) is not a plan-only request and does not arm this.

rules.title: Run the tests before committing a fix
rules.statement: A failure was reported and no test run has come back green this session. Reproduce it with a test if you can, and have a green run before committing the fix.
rules.why: a fix without a reproduction is a guess; the ablation evidence is 8-10 resolve points. What this checks is only that SOME test run was green after the report: it cannot tell a reproduction from any other test, nor a run made before the fix from one made after. So it advises, and never blocks.

rules.title: Fetch before reading origin
rules.statement: origin/* is as old as your last fetch. Fetch first, then diff, log or rebase against it.
rules.why: owed once per session; cheap correctness on every comparison against the base.

rules.title: Subagents never push or open PRs
rules.statement: Report back. The main agent decides what leaves the machine.
rules.why: shared write state is where multi-agent work fails; Copilot fences agents to their own branch for the same reason.

rules.title: Subagents never edit protected paths
rules.statement: That path is outside a delegate's brief. Propose the change in your report.
rules.why: CI, infrastructure and migrations are where a delegate's partial context does the most damage.
rules.seeded_from: protected paths: deploy-touching directories present in the repo

rules.title: Subagents never touch a database
rules.statement: Migrations and database clients run from the main agent only.
rules.why: shared state a delegate cannot see the whole of.
rules.seeded_from: migrations dir: the repo's migration tool, plus the common clients

rules.title: Subagents do not change the environment
rules.statement: A delegate reports a missing dependency. It does not install one.
rules.why: environment changes outlive the delegate and surprise the main agent.

rules.title: Posture: answer with paths
rules.statement: Answer with paths and conclusions, not file contents. Read big files as slices, and grep for a symbol before you think about delegating the search.
rules.why: shapes the plan before the read gate has to fire.

rules.title: Posture: verification order
rules.statement: Verification order: the linter, then the test file you touched, then a wider run before push.
rules.why: the ordering rules enforce it; this line means they rarely have to.

rules.title: Posture: large reviews are delegated
rules.statement: Diffs over 400 lines are reviewed by file or by subagent, one per dimension. You read the stat and the verdicts.
rules.why: names the pattern once so the diff rule is a reminder, not a surprise.

rules.title: Posture: irreversible means ask
rules.statement: Irreversible, production or secret-touching actions stop and ask. RULEBOOK_OVERRIDE='<why>' records the reason when you proceed.
rules.why: explains the gates before the first one fires.

rules.title: Anchor: this repo's heaviest files
rules.statement: These files run to thousands of lines. grep -n the heading or symbol, read that range, or delegate.
rules.why: fires when the name appears in any call, not only on a read.
rules.seeded_from: largest files: the top uniquely-named files by line count

rules.title: Anchor: the migrations workflow
rules.statement: Migrations: generate with `{{mig_generate_hint}}`, check for a single head, apply locally, then push.
rules.why: the whole migration discipline in one line, recalled when the tool name shows up.
rules.seeded_from: migrations dir: the migration tool and its config file

not_rules.instead: Also list them under permissions.deny as Read(...) and in the sandbox's denyRead. A deny holds in every permission mode; a hook does not run under some of them.

not_rules.what: Unit tests that sleep, hit the network or open a real database
not_rules.instead: A CI lint (ratchet) is the zero-context backstop for the two edit rules in Test hygiene.

not_rules.what: One ordering rule per CI check that runs locally
not_rules.instead: The scan lists the candidates under signals.ci.local_checks. Author each with /memhub:create-rule — they are repo-specific and need a live test.

not_rules.what: Reward hacking, scope creep, instruction decay
not_rules.instead: Not fixable by a pattern. Read-only or hidden tests, a model judge on the diff, and dev/prod separation are the controls with evidence behind them.

not_rules.what: Team conventions written in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md
not_rules.instead: Choose "Rules from my own work" (or "Both") in this skill: it imports them with a source_ref per sentence and replays them over real sessions.

not_rules.what: "The latest thing I said wins" (a new plan-only request after an earlier go-ahead)
not_rules.instead: The hook's user predicates are unordered over the session, so this cannot be a pattern today. It needs a turn-scoped predicate in the hook; until then start a new session for the new plan, or say it through /memhub:create-rule as a prompt-armed ordering.

cut.why: Replayed over 140 real sessions it fired 43 times, almost all `grep -rn <symbol> <dir>` — the cheap, correct way to find a symbol. Its advice (delegate the search) costs ~54K tokens per subagent by the catalog's own evidence.
